The '''Quess sector''' was located in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] and contained the [[Old Mankoo system/Legends|Old Mankoo]], [[Sayblohn system/Legends|Sayblohn]], [[Tendo system/Legends|Tendo]], and [[Trevi system/Legends|Trevi systems]] as well as several [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]]. It included the [[Planet/Legends|planets]] [[Old Mankoo]], [[Sayblohn]], and [[Trevi IV]], as well as several worlds in the Tendo [[Star system/Legends|system]], where the [[Death/Legends|murderer]] [[Stalnus]] maintained a network of contacts.

Old Mankoo was an impoverished planet whose [[Royal family of Old Mankoo|royal family]] had been overthrown by [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]], and Trevi IV was a [[Merchant/Legends|trade]] world that was originally [[Colonist/Legends|settled]] by [[Truishii]] traders at least two [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] before the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. The latter planet had a population of thirty-five million beings of various [[Species/Legends|species]]. During the Galactic Civil War, the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] maintained a light presence in the Trevi system, and it also occupied Sayblohn, the [[Desert/Legends|badlands]] of which additionally hosted a [[Sayblohn pirate base|hidden pirate base]].

==Description==
The Quess [[Sector/Legends|sector]] was located in the [[Trailing Sectors/Legends|Trailing Sectors]] portion of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]].<ref name="Trailing" /> By [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], it bordered the [[Mulgard sector/Legends|Mulgard sector]] [[Core Worlds/Legends|Coreward]], the [[Chommell sector/Legends|Chommell]] and [[Vish sector/Legends|Vish sectors]] [[spinward]], and the [[Dustig sector/Legends|Dustig sector]] in the [[trailing]] direction. [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Rimward]], the sector bordered the [[Alui sector/Legends|Alui sector]] as well as forming a part of the Mid Rim's border with the Outer Rim Territories' [[Grumani sector/Legends|Grumani sector]].<ref name="Mid Rim" />

The northernmost section of the Quess sector contained the [[Old Mankoo system/Legends|Old Mankoo]] and [[Sayblohn system/Legends|Sayblohn systems]], while the [[Trevi system/Legends|Trevi system]] lay in the more southward portion of the sector.<ref name="Directions">{{SW|url=news/essential-atlas-extra-sectors-of-the-mid-rim|text=Essential Atlas Extra: Sectors of the Mid Rim}} places the Quess [[Sector/Legends|sector]] [[Star system/Legends|systems]] of [[Old Mankoo system/Legends|Old Mankoo]] and [[Trevi system/Legends|Trevi]] in the northernmost and the more southward sections of the sector, respectively. In addition, {{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} places the [[Sayblohn system/Legends|Sayblohn]] in grid square N-16, which also corresponds to the sector's northernmost part per the former source.</ref> The [[Tendo system/Legends|Tendo system]] was also a part of the sector.<ref name="EAOC" /> The Trevi [[Star system/Legends|system]] was located along several [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] used in interstellar [[Merchant/Legends|commerce]].<ref name="Journal 9" />

==Locations==
The Trevi system contained the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Trevi IV]].<ref name="Journal 9" /> The Old Mankoo and Sayblohn systems<ref name="EAOC" /> included the worlds [[Old Mankoo]]<ref name="Republic 47">[[Republic 47|''Republic'' 47]]</ref> and [[Sayblohn]], respectively,<ref name="RPG2RE">''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> and the Tendo system contained several planets as well.<ref name="Wanted">[[Wanted by Cracken (sourcebook)|''Wanted by Cracken'']]</ref> An impoverished world<ref name="CSWE OldMankoo">{{CSWECite|II|407|Old Mankoo}}</ref> whose [[Royal family of Old Mankoo|royal family]] had been overthrown<ref name="Republic 48">[[Republic 48|''Republic'' 48]]</ref> by [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]],<ref name="23 BBY">''[[Star Wars: The Comics Companion]]'' dates the events of the [[Star Wars: Republic: Honor and Duty|''Honor and Duty'']] story arc of the ''[[Star Wars: Republic]]'' [[Star Wars comic books|comic-book]] series, which includes its [[Republic 48|forty-eighth issue]], to twenty-three [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the events of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], which corresponds to [[23 BBY/Legends|23 BBY]] according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.</ref> Old Mankoo was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the<ref name="Republic 48" /> [[Human/Legends|Human]]<ref name="Republic 47" /> [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Tsian]],<ref name="Republic 48" /> who eventually left the planet for the wider [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]].<ref name="Republic 47" /> By [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]],<ref name="7 ABY">[[Wanted by Cracken (sourcebook)|''Wanted by Cracken'']] is dated to three [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]. Since ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates that conflict to [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the placement of the sourcebook therefore translates to [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]].</ref> the [[Riorian/Legends|Riorian]] [[Death/Legends|murderer]] [[Stalnus]] frequented the worlds of the Tendo system, in which he maintained a network of contacts.<ref name="Wanted" />

[[File:Trevi-TEA.png|thumb|left|300px|The Quess sector contained, among others, the Old Mankoo and Trevi systems.]]
Trevi IV was a dry planet of barren plains, [[Desert/Legends|deserts]], plateaus, and [[City/Legends|urbanized]] areas. At some point, a caravan of [[Truishii]] traders passing the Trevi system experienced an accident in [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]], and a Truishii [[Starship/Legends|starship]] landed on Trevi IV so that it could be repaired. The traders decided to establish a [[Colonist/Legends|colony]] on the planet, and it rapidly developed into a [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] settlement known as [[Trevi City]].<ref name="Journal 9" />

Trevi IV eventually became a trade world inhabited by thirty-five million [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] beings of various [[Species/Legends|species]], including Humans and [[Alien/Legends|aliens]] from a thousand worlds. The inhabitants of Trevi IV imported [[Foodstuff/Legends|foodstuffs]] and medical supplies on their homeworld while exporting luxury goods and technology to the rets of the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]. Slightly more than twenty [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the [[Bith/Legends|Bith]] entrepreneur [[Fiz Cor'gril]] also arrived on the planet and established in Trevi City a used starship dealership called [[Fizzi's Slightly Used Starships]]. During the Galactic Civil War, a small post located just outside Trevi City constituted the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] token presence both on Trevi IV and in its [[Star/Legends|star]] system.<ref name="Journal 9" />

{{RPGseed}}
A world with a [[Sayblohn pirate base|pirate base]] hidden in its badlands, Sayblohn was occupied by the Empire during the Galactic Civil War. At some point during that conflict,<ref name="RPG2RE" /> a [[Alliance Special Operations/Legends|special operative team]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|406|Okfili}}</ref> traveled to Sayblohn to retrieve a [[Thief/Legends|stolen]] [[Okfili art object|art object]] that held significant religious importance to the [[Okfili]] species. On the planet, the [[operative]]s eventually retrieved the artifact from the [[Unidentified pirate group (Sayblohn)|local pirate group]] and [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggled]] it onto their starship without attracting Imperial attention.<ref name="RPG2RE" />
{{Endgame}}

==Behind the scenes==
The Quess sector was established in "[[Fizzi's Slightly Used Starships (article)|Fizzi's Slightly Used Starships]]," a [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game|roleplaying game]] source article written by [[John J. Richardson III]] and published in [[February]] [[1996]] in the [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 9|ninth issue]] of [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars Adventure Journal]]''.<ref name="Journal 9" /> In [[2012]], the sector was depicted on a map designed by [[Modi]] and published in "[https://www.starwars.com/news/essential-atlas-extra-sectors-of-the-mid-rim Essential Atlas Extra: Sectors of the Mid Rim]," a feature of the [[StarWars.com]] [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|Online Companion]]<ref name="Mid Rim" /> to the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]''<ref name="EAOC" /> that placed it in grid squares N-16 and N-17.<ref name="Mid Rim" />
